essays.stem: Explain how you would work out the materials to buy for rewiring a three-bedroom house, from the drawings to the final order list.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start with the latest drawings, the specification and the circuit schedule. I would count every accessory from the drawings, room by room: switches, outlets, light points, boxes and the board with its breakers. I would measure each cable run on the drawing using the scale, adding the drops down walls and the extra needed at each end, and total the length for each cable size. I would do the same for conduit, fittings and fixings. Then I would add an allowance for waste, such as 10%, and round up to the pack sizes the suppliers sell, for example 100 m rolls or 3 m lengths. I would check what is already in our store so we do not buy twice. Finally I would write a clear list with each item's description, size, rating, quantity and unit, and have a second person check it.
markingPoints: Uses the latest drawings, specification and circuit schedule
Counts accessories and measures cable runs to scale, including drops and ends
Adds a waste allowance and rounds up to pack sizes
Checks existing stock
Writes a clear, checked list with description, size, rating, quantity and unit

essays.stem: Describe how you would get and compare quotations from three suppliers for a large order of cable and breakers, and how you would choose.
essays.modelAnswer: I would send the same written enquiry to three approved suppliers, listing each item with its exact description, size, rating and quantity, the delivery place and the date needed, and ask for a written quotation by a set date. When the quotes come back I would put them side by side in a table. I would check that each one quotes exactly the items asked for, and note any substitutes. I would compare the unit prices, any discounts, whether GCT is included, delivery charges, lead times, payment terms and warranty. I would also think about each supplier's past record for correct and on-time delivery and the quality of their goods. The cheapest is not always best: an offer that arrives too late or is not to the specification is not suitable. I would record the reason for my choice and get the order approved.
markingPoints: Sends the same detailed enquiry to approved suppliers
Compares quotes side by side and checks they match the specification
Compares price, discount, GCT, delivery, lead time, terms and warranty
Considers past performance; cheapest is not always best
Records the reason and gets approval

essays.stem: Explain what information must be on a purchase order for electrical materials, and why each part matters.
essays.modelAnswer: A purchase order needs the firm's name and address and a unique order number, so the order, delivery note and invoice can be matched. It needs the supplier's name and the quotation number, so the agreed prices apply. Each line needs a clear description with size, rating, type and part number, the quantity and the unit, so the right item arrives. It shows the unit price and the total, with GCT shown separately at the current rate, so the cost can be checked against the budget and the invoice. It gives the delivery address, the date needed and a contact person, so somebody is there to receive and check the goods. It gives the job number for costing, and the payment terms. Finally it is signed by a person allowed to approve that amount, so the firm controls spending.
markingPoints: Unique order number and supplier and quote details for matching
Clear description, size, rating, part number, quantity and unit
Prices, total and GCT shown separately for checking
Delivery address, date and contact; job number; terms
Signed by an authorised person

essays.stem: Describe how you would receive and check a delivery of electrical materials on site, and what you would do about shortages or damage.
essays.modelAnswer: I would have a copy of the purchase order ready and make sure the area for unloading is clear and safe. When the goods arrive I would check the delivery note against the order, then count each item and check sizes, ratings and markings, such as the cable size printed on the sheath. I would look for damage to boxes, drums and items. If everything is correct I would sign the delivery note. If there is a shortage, a wrong item or damage, I would write it clearly on the delivery note before signing, take photos, and keep the faulty items apart and tagged. I would tell the purchaser at once so they can contact the supplier for a replacement or a credit note. I would record what was received, store the goods safely and pass the signed paperwork to the office for the invoice check.
markingPoints: Has the order ready and a safe unloading area
Checks delivery note against order; counts and checks sizes, ratings and markings
Looks for damage; signs only when checked
Notes shortages or damage on the note, photographs, separates faulty items and tells the purchaser
Records, stores safely and passes paperwork for the invoice check

essays.stem: Explain why it is dangerous to buy breakers, cable or accessories of unknown origin, and how a purchaser can avoid fake or poor-quality goods.
essays.modelAnswer: Fake or poor-quality items can look like the real thing but fail when they are needed. A fake breaker may not trip on overload or fault, so a cable can overheat and start a fire. Cable with thin copper or poor insulation can overheat or break down and give shocks. Poor accessories can crack, loosen and arc. The firm could be blamed for injury or damage, and the work could fail inspection. To avoid them, the purchaser buys only from approved suppliers with a good record, and is wary of prices that are far below normal. She asks for items with recognised approval marks and the maker's details, checks the markings and packaging on delivery, and compares weight and finish with known good items. Any doubtful item is quarantined and reported, not used.
markingPoints: Fake breakers may not trip, causing fire
Poor cable or accessories can overheat, give shocks or arc
Firm liability and failed inspection
Buy from approved suppliers; be wary of very low prices; ask for approval marks
Check items on delivery and quarantine doubtful items

essays.stem: Explain how you would plan the timing of purchases on a ten-week job so that materials arrive when needed without crowding the site.
essays.modelAnswer: I would look at the job programme and list when each stage needs its materials: conduit and boxes for first fix, cable for wiring, the board, accessories and light fittings for second fix. I would find each item's lead time from the suppliers. Items with long lead times, such as a special board or imported fittings, I would order as soon as the design is approved. For common items I would arrange deliveries in stages, called off a few days before each stage, so the site does not fill up and goods are not stolen or damaged. I would allow a few days' margin for late deliveries. I would put the order dates and delivery dates on a simple schedule, check it each week against progress, and move deliveries if the programme changes.
markingPoints: Links materials to the stages of the programme
Finds lead times and orders long-lead items early
Calls off common items in stages to save space and reduce loss
Allows a margin for late deliveries
Keeps an order and delivery schedule and reviews it with progress

essays.stem: Explain the 'three-way match' and why it protects the firm when paying suppliers.
essays.modelAnswer: The three-way match means checking three documents against each other before an invoice is paid: the purchase order, which shows what was agreed; the delivery note or goods-received record, which shows what actually arrived and was accepted; and the supplier's invoice, which shows what the supplier is asking to be paid. The items, quantities and prices must agree on all three. If the invoice charges for 10 drums but only 8 were received, or the price is higher than the order, the difference is queried with the supplier before payment. This protects the firm from paying for goods it never received, wrong prices, duplicate invoices or items that were returned. It also helps find errors in the store and keeps good records for audits.
markingPoints: Names the three documents: order, delivery record, invoice
Items, quantities and prices must agree
Differences are queried before paying
Protects against paying for goods not received, wrong prices or duplicates
Supports records and audits

essays.stem: Describe the ethical rules a purchaser should follow when dealing with suppliers, and why they matter.
essays.modelAnswer: A purchaser spends the firm's money, so she must act in the firm's interest, not her own. She should not accept gifts, cash or favours that could affect her choice, and should report any offer to her manager. If a friend or family member owns a supplier, she should say so and let someone else decide. She should treat all suppliers fairly, give each the same information, and not share one supplier's prices with another to gain an advantage. She should keep honest records and never split orders to avoid the approval limit. She should keep to the firm's purchasing procedure. These rules matter because they keep prices fair, protect the firm from fraud and loss, keep the trust of suppliers and clients, and protect the purchaser's own reputation.
markingPoints: Acts in the firm's interest; refuses and reports gifts
Declares conflicts of interest
Treats suppliers fairly and keeps prices confidential
Keeps honest records; does not split orders; follows procedure
Explains why: fair prices, no fraud, trust and reputation

essays.stem: Explain how a purchaser keeps spending within the materials budget for a job, and what to do if costs start to rise.
essays.modelAnswer: At the start I would get the materials budget from the estimate and break it down by main item. Each time an order is approved I would add it to a running total, with GCT and delivery, and compare it with the budget for that item. I would check invoices against orders so no extra charges slip in. I would control waste by ordering from an accurate take-off, issuing materials against job cards and returning unused items to the store or supplier. If costs start to rise, for example because of price increases, waste or extra work, I would find the cause and tell my supervisor early, with figures. Together we might look for other approved suppliers, agree a cheaper item that still meets the specification, or price the extra work as a variation for the client.
markingPoints: Breaks the budget down and keeps a running total of orders
Checks invoices against orders
Controls waste: accurate take-off, issue against job cards, returns
Finds the cause of rising costs and reports early with figures
Suggests actions: other suppliers, approved alternatives, variations

essays.stem: Describe how you would set up simple stock control for the firm's store of common electrical items, so that they do not run out or go to waste.
essays.modelAnswer: I would list the common items we keep, such as cable, breakers, outlets, boxes, conduit and fixings, with a code and a fixed shelf place for each. Each item gets a stock card or a spreadsheet line showing what comes in and what goes out. For each item I would set a reorder level, worked out from how many we use each week, the supplier's lead time and a small safety stock, so we reorder before running out. Items are issued only against a job card, and the oldest stock is used first. I would store goods safely: drums off the floor and under cover, small parts in labelled bins. Every month I would count the stock, compare it with the records and look into any difference. I would also review slow-moving items so we do not keep buying things we rarely use.
markingPoints: Lists items with codes and fixed places
Keeps stock cards or a spreadsheet of in and out
Sets reorder levels from usage, lead time and safety stock
Issues against job cards, oldest first; stores safely
Counts regularly, checks differences and reviews slow movers

practical1.title: Take-off, quotation comparison and purchase order for a small installation
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a drawing and specification for a two-room extension (lighting, socket outlets, an A/C supply and a small board), price sheets from three made-up suppliers with their lead times and terms, the firm's approval limits and a materials budget. As a purchasing team: (1) do a full take-off from the drawing, measuring cable and conduit runs to scale; (2) add a waste allowance and round up to the suppliers' pack sizes; (3) write an enquiry; (4) compare the three suppliers in a table on price, discount, delivery, lead time, terms and warranty; (5) choose a supplier for each item and write down why; (6) write a purchase order with GCT shown as a separate line at the rate the assessor gives; (7) check the total against the budget and send the order for approval to the right person (the assessor). Each member does the take-off for one part of the job and checks another member's part. Photograph each stage and hand in all the documents.
materials: Drawing and specification of the extension (from the assessor)
Price sheets, lead times and terms from three made-up suppliers
Take-off sheets, comparison table, enquiry form and purchase order forms
Computer with a spreadsheet (if available) and a phone or camera for photos
photos: The marked-up drawing used for the take-off
The completed take-off sheet with waste allowance
The written reasons for the choice of supplier
The finished purchase order with GCT shown separately
The budget check and approval request
checklist: Measured runs to scale and counted accessories accurately for their part
Added a sensible waste allowance and rounded up to pack sizes
Compared suppliers on more than price, and gave clear reasons
Wrote order lines with full descriptions, sizes, ratings, quantities and units
Calculated totals and GCT correctly at the rate given
Checked the total against the budget and followed the approval limit
Checked another member's take-off and corrected any errors
safety: This is a desk task: keep bags and cables off the floor and walkways
Use the computer and phone safely and sit with good posture
Keep supplier prices and the firm's budget confidential
Follow the Centre's rules for the classroom

practical2.title: Receive, check and record a delivery against the purchase order
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up a mock delivery of electrical materials with a purchase order, a delivery note and the supplier's invoice. The assessor has built in problems: a short count, a wrong breaker rating, a damaged box of accessories, a missing safety data sheet for a solvent cement, and an invoice price that differs from the order. As a receiving team: (1) prepare a safe unloading and checking area; (2) check the delivery note against the order; (3) count and inspect each item and read its markings; (4) note every problem on the delivery note before signing, and photograph it; (5) tag and set aside wrong and damaged items; (6) fill in a goods-received note and update the stock cards; (7) do a three-way match of order, goods-received note and invoice; and (8) write a short message to the supplier asking for replacements or a credit note. Each member checks one group of items, and one member leads the three-way match. Photograph each stage and hand in all documents.
materials: Mock delivery of electrical materials with built-in problems (from the assessor)
Purchase order, delivery note and supplier's invoice
Goods-received note forms, stock cards and reject tags
Trolley or sack truck for moving boxes
Clipboards, pens, calculators and a phone or camera for photos
photos: The unloading and checking area set out
Items being counted and markings checked against the order
Problems written on the delivery note
Wrong and damaged items tagged and set aside
The completed goods-received note and stock cards
The three-way match and the message to the supplier
checklist: Set out a safe, clear checking area
Counted and checked items, sizes and ratings against the order
Found the built-in problems in their group of items
Recorded problems on the delivery note before signing
Completed the goods-received note and stock cards correctly
Did or checked the three-way match and found the price difference
safety: Lift safely: bend the knees, keep the load close, and get help or use a trolley for heavy items
Keep walkways and exits clear while the goods are checked
Handle damaged boxes with gloves, watching for broken parts and sharp edges
Keep solvent cement closed, away from heat, and store it as its safety data sheet says
